headline: Pew Research Study Projects Future Religious Demographics In India
seoTitle: Pew Research Data On Future Religious Demographics In India
metaDescription: A new Pew Research Center report examines projected population changes for religious groups in India and globally, including shifts in Hindu and Muslim…
aiSummaryBullets: New projections from the Pew Research Center indicate India will maintain a majority Hindu population in the coming decades.
Data suggests that the Muslim population within India is expected to experience a faster growth rate compared to other groups.
Global estimates indicate the total number of Hindus is expected to rise to 1.4 billion by 2070 while global Muslim populations will grow.
aiContextParagraph: The Pew Research Center has released demographic data projecting the future religious composition of India and the world. According to the research, India is anticipated to remain a nation with a predominant Hindu majority in the long term. However, the study identifies varying growth rates among different religious communities, noting that the Muslim population in India is projected to increase at a faster pace than other groups. On a global scale, the report forecasts that the absolute number of Hindus worldwide will grow from 1.2 billion in 2020 to approximately 1.4 billion by the year 2070. Furthermore, researchers expect the total global population of Muslims to exceed the number of Christians by 2035. These projections are based on ongoing demographic analysis of religious trends, providing a long-term outlook on how population structures may shift across various regions and faith groups in the next several decades.
whyItIsViral: The topic is currently being discussed across two independent media outlets, reflecting moderate interest in the latest demographic research findings.
